question.problem: A right triangle has legs of length $\frac{\sqrt{20}}{3}$ and $\frac{4}{3}.$ Calculate the length of its hypotenuse.
question.worked_solution:
Let $a=\frac{\sqrt{20}}{3},$ $b=\frac{4}{3},$ and $c$ be the length of the hypotenuse. According to the Pythagorean theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}^{2} & ={a}^{2}+{b}^{2} \\ c & =\sqrt{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting in the values for $a$ and $b$ gives us

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\sqrt{20}}{3})}^{2}+{(\frac{4}{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{20}{9}+\frac{16}{9}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{36}{9}} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
